cards.text: After this, Samuel calls the people together to the LORD at Mizpah. Samuel is Israel's prophet, and he's got a message for the whole crowd. It comes straight from the LORD, the God of Israel.

cards.question: The LORD's message to Israel at Mizpah starts with a reminder. What does He say He did for them?

answers.text: Brought them up out of Egypt
Gave them a king long ago
Built them a city at Mizpah

cards.text: Then the message turns. The LORD is the God who saves them from all their troubles, and they told Him, 'No, set a king over us.'

cards.question: Right alongside that demand for a king, the LORD names something Israel has done today. What is it?

cards.text: Samuel has Israel present themselves before the LORD by tribes and clans, so all the tribes come forward. I know this feeling, friend: YEARS in a junk drawer, holding my breath every time it opened to see who was getting picked.

cards.question: All the tribes of Israel come forward before the LORD. Which tribe is selected?
Next the tribe of Benjamin comes forward clan by clan, and the clan of Matri is selected. Then one man is selected. Who is it?
Saul son of Kish is selected, and they go looking for him. What happens?

cards.text: The man just got selected, and NOBODY can find him. So they inquire of the LORD again: 'Has the man come here yet?'

cards.question: The LORD answers their question about the missing man. Where is Saul?

cards.text: The brand new pick, tucked in with the baggage. No judgment here, friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, and I never even got a crowd looking for me.

cards.question: They run and bring Saul out to stand among the people. What does everybody see?

answers.text: He's a head taller than everyone

cards.text: Then Samuel says to all the people, “Do you see the one the LORD has chosen? There is no one like him among all the people.” That is a BIG introduction for a man they just pulled out of the luggage.

cards.question: Samuel presents Saul as the one the LORD has chosen. How do all the people respond?

answers.text: They cheer for their new king
They ask for a different man

cards.text: Then Samuel explains the rights of kingship to the people. The king's job description, spelled out for the whole crowd.

cards.question: Samuel explains the rights of kingship to the people, but he never writes them down.
Samuel sends everyone home, and Saul heads to his home in Gibeah too. Who goes with him?

cards.text: But not everybody's on board. Some worthless men say, “How can this man save us?”

cards.question: Those worthless men despise Saul and bring him no gifts. How does Saul respond?

answers.text: He calls them out in public

cards.text: Not one word from the new king. And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because this king's story is far from over.

findings.problem: The card tells the start of the LORD's message to the Israelites ('he's got a message for the whole crowd. It comes straight from the LORD, the God of Israel'), which is in 1 Samuel 10:18. The card cites only 1 Samuel 10:17. It should cite 1 Samuel 10:17-18.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Card 3 already says the people told the God who saves them, 'No, set a king over us.' That rules out 'Obeyed their God' and 'Thanked their God,' so the right answer 'Rejected their God' is given away. Neither wrong answer is believable after that setup.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card opens by retelling that nobody can find the man who was selected, which is 1 Samuel 10:21. The card cites only 1 Samuel 10:22. It should cite 1 Samuel 10:21-22.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: This story card tells nothing new from the passage. It repeats card 10's answer (Saul hidden among the baggage) only to carry a joke. It is also the second junk drawer 'YEARS' joke in the stop, after card 5. Either cut the card or fold the joke into a card that moves the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards. ... Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: Of the 11 choice cards, 10 are multiple choice, 1 is true or false, and none is fill in the blank. Multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Many choice cards are pure discovery with no story card context to reason from. Card 6 (which tribe), card 8 (what happens when they look for Saul), card 10 (where he is hidden), card 12 (what people see) and card 17 (who goes with Saul) can only be answered by luck. That is close to half of the 11 choice cards. Add context on the story cards before some of them, or ask questions the baker can reason out.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: No card tells that Samuel laid the scroll up before the LORD (1 Samuel 10:25). Card 16 covers only that the rights of kingship were written down, so the baker leaves without this detail.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
